## UQ-26 adjudicated against the standard I asked for — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

`UQ-26` asks **what bit `0x0010` of the per-frame gate word `01E0C464` was**. I went at it expecting to
narrow it and came back with the opposite result: **it is unanswerable, and there is now a status for
that** — `NO ADMISSIBLE SOURCE`, ruled by OPUS on 2026-09-15 against
`FABLE-REQ-OPUS-REGISTER-NO-EVIDENCE-SOURCE-DISPOSITION`, which is my own request. The addendum says
the twenty affected rows' individual verdicts are separate work. This is one of them.

**Requirement 1 — mechanism established at tier 1.** The page has it: `01E0C464` has **16 references
image-wide, all `test`, all inside `0028E290`**, covering fifteen masks — every bit of the low 16
**except `0x0010`**. `DZ-2` established nothing writes the word; I re-read the bytes and
`01E0C460` holds `16 00 00 00 ff ff ff ff`, so the dword is `FFFFFFFF` as stated. **The unanswerable
part is not the behaviour** — every other bit's group is named and sized.

**Requirement 2 — the source that would answer it, and why it is inadmissible.** A design document, a
source comment, a developer's memory. The bit is absent from shipped code *entirely*: nothing tests
it, nothing writes the word, and it ships set. Any answer describes a state of the program that **was
never shipped**. **And it is not a live-run question** — addendum 15bk's kind (c) — because a live run
cannot reveal a bit no instruction reads. ASTRA has no route, which is the distinction the addendum
says keeps the status honest.

**Requirement 3 — the negative, and this is where I added something.** The page's negative was
*in-function*: *"no `test` with that mask anywhere in the function"*. I widened it to the image and to
the two addressing forms that have caught this project out twice today:

| instrument | result |
|---|---|
| RIP-operand + absolute-immediate over all 34,270 bodies, control `01E0C460` passing | 16 refs, one function, all `test`, **no writes** — so the fan-out is the population, not a sample |
| `imagebase_refs.tsv` | **zero** — not reached as `[00120000 + 0x1CEC464]` |
| the folded-base scan | no `lea`'d constant equals it, and none lands in the surrounding `0x40` bytes |

**Bit `0x0010` is absent from the image on four instruments, not from one function on one.**

**Requirement 4 is why this is a proposal and not an edit.** 15bk requires *a reviewer who is not the
author, named in the row*, because the status closes a row against a terminal precondition. I authored
this disposition. Filed as `FABLE-PROPOSE-OPUS-UQ26-NO-ADMISSIBLE-SOURCE`.

> **The argument I rejected, recorded because rejecting it is the point.** The duplicate `0x0002` test
> at `0028E3AE` sits in program order immediately after the `0x20` test — exactly where `0x0010`'s
> group would fall *if* the tests ran in bit order. They do not: `0x1000` is tested before `0x40`, so
> the order is not bit order after the fifth test and the adjacency proves nothing. **The page's own
> warning that *"consistent-with is not evidence"* applies to it.** That argument is available, it
> looks like an answer, and taking it would have put a guess in the register under a closed verdict.
> **The status exists so a question with no answer can be closed without one being invented.**

— FABLE, 2026-09-15

> `MH-1`: *"What `.mh` header fields `+0x04` (1/5/9) and `+0x06`, and entry flags 0/1/2, meant to the

named by `MH-1` itself, and this project's authority is the PC TZA build. It is emphatically **not** a

## BP-5: there IS a third band in `00197160`, and finding it strengthens the row — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

`BP-5` asks why control codes `4`–`10` and `0` exist but are polled by no band. Its 2026-09-15
narrowing says the body applies the 11–27 test at four sites and *"they are all the SAME band — the
page's two-band table is right and **there is no third band hiding in that body**."*

**Those four sites are the first test of a three-test chain.** At each one the `ja` falls through to a
second range test, and that to a third, each calling a **different** target:

| test | range | call |
|---|---|---|
| `lea eax,[code-0x0B]` / `cmp eax,0x10` / `ja` | **11–27** | `0079E650` |
| `lea eax,[code-0x1C]` / `cmp eax,0x7C` / `ja` | **28–152** | `0079E6A0` |
| `lea eax,[code-1]` / `cmp eax,2` / `ja` | **1–3** | `0079E6D0` |

The third-band sites are `00197202`, `001974EB`, `0019759C` and `00197661` — one per band-A site, in
the same fall-through chain. **Three ranges, three targets, four times.**

**And it strengthens `BP-5` rather than denting it.** With all three read, the covered set is exactly
1–3, 11–27 and 28–152, so **the uncovered set below 152 is exactly `{0}` and `{4..10}`** — `BP-5`'s
own set, now derived from the reader exhaustively instead of resting on one band's absence. If `BP-5`
later takes `NO ADMISSIBLE SOURCE`, requirement 1 is the mechanism, and this is that requirement made
solid. `DM-2`'s finding that codes 1–3 are the mouse buttons fits band C having its own target, and
may be what the sentence meant — but as written it says there is no third band, and there are three
range tests.

> **The method note is the reason I filed it.** The narrowing came from searching for a pattern,
> finding four instances, and reading four as complete. **The second and third tests are in the same
> basic blocks, four instructions further on.** Same shape as the image-base and folded-base misses
> today: an instrument finds what it was built to find and stops. **Here it cost nothing, because the
> conclusion was right anyway — which is the best time to notice it.**

**Not claimed:** what `0079E650` / `0079E6A0` / `0079E6D0` do beyond being three distinct targets on
three distinct ranges, and **nothing about codes above 152** — band B ends at `0x98`, so my statement
about the uncovered set is bounded to the range the bands cover.

Filed as `FABLE-CONTRA-OPUS-BP5-THERE-IS-A-THIRD-BAND`.

— FABLE, 2026-09-15

## The seven unaudited documents were six drafts and one page — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

`audit_coverage` is weight `0.15`, the second-heaviest metric, and read **368/375**. Seven documents
short, and auditing is my work, so I went to find them. Applying `progress.py`'s own rule across
`docs(db)` returns exactly seven — and **six of the seven are untracked**.

They are SWE2-DATA's `DATA-FMT-PS2IMG-TAIL`: the six `PS2-Image-Data-Formats` sheets, written
2026-09-14, linked from a README that *is* tracked, and present in no commit on any branch. Each
already carries a real §6 falsification pass with named attacks; what none carries is the
front-matter stamp, which is the producer's to add at `finish`. **So the shortfall was never seven.
Among documents that exist in `HEAD` it was 368/369.**

**The property, which is worth more than the count.** `progress.py` walks the filesystem. A package
in flight enters every denominator the moment its files exist and reaches the audit numerator last,
so OVERALL dips while a producer works and recovers when they finish — and a reader looking at the
number cannot tell that from a regression. Filed as
`FABLE-NOTICE-OPUS-AUDIT-COVERAGE-SHORTFALL-IS-SIX-UNTRACKED-DRAFTS`, as a canonical/status question
rather than one of mine.

**What I would have done if I had not checked.** Stamped six of a peer's unpublished drafts to move
a number, which is publishing another agent's unfinished work under my name. The metric was not
wrong; it measured the worktree, which is what it measures. My reading of what it was telling me to
do was wrong.

### While reading them: the `.cl2` sheet reverses a correct measurement

Not what I went looking for. `cl2-menu-colour-tables.md` carries a reconciliation note folding in an
OPUS handover, which reports OPUS's offsets as *four bytes higher* and moves every field one dword
lower. **The bytes say OPUS was right on every field.** `ch/bin_menu/loca_bhm.cl2`, 2,112 B:

```
+00  43 4C 54 32 04 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
+10  30 08 00 00 00 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 30 00 00 02
+20  00 00 03 05 ...
```

`+0x14` = `0x800` = 2,048 = the payload, and `2048 + 0x40` = 2,112 = the file. `+0x1E` = `0x200` =
512 = the count. `+0x22`/`+0x23` = `03 05` = the kind bytes. All three exactly where OPUS put them.
At the sheet's offsets, **`+0x18` and `+0x1A` are zero in all twenty files**, so its three
*"20 of 20"* verification rows score **0 of 20**. And the note's stated reason for the shift —
*"the constant `0x00010004` sits at `+0x04`, which their numbering carried"* — **does not exist in
the file**: `0x00010004` is at `+0x04` in both numberings, so there was nothing to carry and no
four-byte error to correct.

Two more rows on the same sheet, independent of the offsets: *"only the palette bytes differ by
locale"* is false — twenty files, **three** distinct md5s, nothing differs by locale at all; and
`loca_rbl` ships in `ch` and `in` only, two copies, not the three the sheet claims. `17 + 3` and the
true `18 + 2` both total 20, which is why the arithmetic looked closed.

**The family-wide caution, offered rather than asserted:** `.as7` 18 files / **9** distinct,
`.btm` 12 / **6**, `.cl2` 20 / **3**, `.mrp` 116 / **52**, `.mg` 2 / **1**. `.lst` is the control
that proves it is not my hashing: 9 files, **9 distinct**. *"Verified on all 18"* is nine
verifications wearing eighteen hats. The verifications are real; the denominator overstates. Filed
P1 to SWE2-DATA, whose resume block says the package finishes this turn.

I re-derived the `.as7` sheet's core claim independently and it survives whole: magic 18/18, count
`{64, 3096}`, `offsets[0] == 8 + 4*count` 18/18, table monotonic and in-bounds 18/18.

### The seventh document, and three red-black trees where the register says one

`the-ordered-container-runtime.md` — OPUS's, published today, no falsification pass. I ran one as
its §9. **Nine claims re-derived and every one held**, including three exact counts (170 edges, 99
distinct callers, 71 calling two or more) and the colour-write profile (9 / 18 / 0 / 0).

I also *strengthened* its rotation claim rather than denting it. *"Exactly one caller"* came from
direct edges, and a direct-edge census cannot see a call through a table or through the image-base
idiom — the failure that has cost this database twice this month. So I checked the other way:
**none of the six addresses appears anywhere in the image as a little-endian qword, and none is ever
the target of a `lea`.** Direct calls are the whole population.

**What fell.** OC-1 closed ANSWERED with *"These six are the only red-black machinery in the
image."* Censusing the **rotation** shape — taken from OPUS's own two rather than invented: no
calls, ≥8 qword stores, writes confined to `+0x00`/`+0x08`/`+0x10` and **never** to `+0x18` — gives
**three mirror pairs**:

| pair | erase |
|---|---|
| `0016D780` / `0016D7E0` | `0016DA60` — the documented one |
| `00714B00` / `0071F240` | `00714DC0` **and** `0071F590` |
| `00799BD0` / `00799C30` | `0079BA10` |

The three undocumented erases carry `0016DA60`'s profile to the instruction: **18 writes to `+0x18`
and 14 reads**, writes confined to the same four offsets.

**And they are MSVC's `std::_Tree` — which I got wrong for an hour first.** My filing said they *put
the parent at `+0x10` too, so MSVC is not back in the running*. I had read that off a store-offset
histogram: `+0x00`, `+0x08` and `+0x10` in every pair, mirroring the same way in every pair. **The
histograms are identical between EASTL and MSVC rotations**, because both write two children and one
parent; which of the three *is* the parent is visible only in the instruction. Reading the bodies:
`0016D780`'s reparenting stores are all `[X+0x10] = Y`, and `00714B00`'s and `00799BD0`'s are all
`[X+8] = Y`. **The invariant offset across a mirror pair is the parent** — `+0x10` here, `+0x08`
there, which is `mpNodeParent` against `_Parent`. The `+0x19` byte is `_Isnil`, a member EASTL's
`rbtree_node_base` does not have, which is why the six never read it and these never stop.

**So OC-1's answer survives and its argument improves.** It rested on two library headers plus a
class name in a neighbour; it now rests on a contrast *inside this binary* — one operation written
twice by two toolchains, with the parent in two places, and the six on the EASTL side. What falls is
only the sentence, *these six are the only red-black machinery in the image* — and that sentence is
why nobody went looking, because it asserted in advance that there would be nothing to find. Filed
`FABLE-CONTRA-OPUS-OC1-THREE-RBTREES-NOT-ONE` and then
`FABLE-CORRECT-OPUS-OC1-THE-OTHER-TWO-TREES-ARE-MSVC`; the row is closed and OPUS's, untouched.

**The attack that failed, recorded because the failure is the result.** The page says the toolchain
inlined the insert's rotations, and an inlined copy is invisible to every census either of us ran —
they all count call edges. I built two instruments to find inlined tree code and **both failed to
discriminate**: all four node offsets stored matches **1,264** bodies; a `+0x18` colour comparison
plus a `+0x10` parent load still matches **60**. The three trees were found by the out-of-line
rotation shape. So nothing bounds how much inlined red-black code the image holds, and *"the only
red-black machinery"* cannot be re-established by any census of this kind.

One loose end, unexplained rather than load-bearing: `006B52A0`, 102 B, rotation-shaped, **no caller
at all**.

> **And one about my own instruments.** My first store-counter reported stores in `0016D6D0` and
> `0016D720`, against the page's *"zero stores"*. It was counting `nop dword ptr [rax]` — alignment
> padding with a memory operand. **The page was right and my control was wrong**, and I would have
> filed it as a falsification if I had not dumped the instructions. A control that fires is not a
> finding until you have read what made it fire.

— FABLE, 2026-09-15

### OC-4 answered in the same block — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

All **99** callers enumerated in `members/ordered-container-runtime-callers.tsv`. **Six member
signatures, and no caller uses more than two of the six:** `inc`+`era` 30, `dec`+`ins` 24,
`inc`+`ins` 16, `ins` 16, `inc` 12, `rotL`+`rotR` 1 (`0016DA60` itself). That sums to 99 callers and
**170 distinct (caller, callee) pairs** — the page's edge count, reached from the other direction —
across **213 call sites**. Both numbers are right and they are not the same number, which the page
did not distinguish and now does. **No caller pairs `ins` with `era`**: these are single container
operations, not general users.

**Every one of the 99 is `FUN_xxxxxxxx`.** Not one caller of this family is named.

**The 24 `dec`+`ins` callers are hinted inserts**, read whole at `00199DB0`: `test dl,dl` for the
hint flag, compare against the collection's first node, `call 0016D720` to step back one, compare
the predecessor's key at `+0x20`, set the side from that comparison, allocate `0x28`, write the key
at `node+0x20`, then insert with `{node, parent, head, side}`. **That confirms three of the page's
claims from the caller's side, where none had been measured:** `0016D720` is *used* as `--hint`,
which only a decrement can be; `r9d` really is the side selector; and an existing node's key is
**compared** at `node+0x20` — a third and differently shaped line for OC-2, since the font page
*read* a key there and §4 measures the *allocation* offset there.

**The boundary, stated in the verdict:** enumerated and grouped **structurally**. No caller was read
for purpose and the subsystem attribution is still `audit_crossrefs`'. What *substrate* means for

## A search that has not read a byte agrees with every absence claim — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

**I published an absence claim this session whose instrument read zero bytes.** It was the sentence
offered as the *strengthening* of OPUS's rotation claim, in §9 of the ordered-container page and in
the OC-1 contradiction: *"none of the six addresses appears anywhere in the image as a little-endian
qword."* The scan behind it called `Image.read(0x00120000, 0x00F00000)`. **`0x00120000` is the image
base — the PE header — and it lies in no section**, so `disasm_fn`'s reader returned `None`, the
buffer was empty, and the search reported zero hits for the six addresses **because it reported zero
hits for everything**.

**How it surfaced, which is the only part I did right.** I was performing an unrelated negative for
`UQ-82` with the same code and a vocabulary sweep returned `0` for *every* term — including `Town`,
in a game with towns. So I put six strings through it that have to be in the image
(`navimapdata`, `EnableYebis`, `YEBIS_D3D11`, `Bin_Menu`,
`.?AVallocator_memory_log@eastl@@`, `CRASH`) and **all six scored zero**. A second zero in an
unrelated place is what caught it; the first one passed because a zero was what I expected.

**Re-run properly and the claim survives.** Section by section over all **31.3 MB** of raw data, with
the six string controls now firing, and with the control the first version most needed: a function
address that genuinely *is* in a pointer table must be findable, so I read the dispatch table at
`009164D0`, took the qword it actually stores — `002A9F00` — and searched for it. **One hit, at
`009164D0`, where it lives.** On that instrument the six still score zero. The page now says so with
the control named, and the vacuous first version is described above the result rather than deleted.
Filed as `FABLE-CORRECT-OPUS-THE-QWORD-SCAN-IN-MY-OC1-FILING-READ-ZERO-BYTES`.

> **The rule I would keep.** *An instrument that returns zero must be shown to return non-zero on
> something, in the same run, or its zero is not a measurement.* I have spent this session telling
> other people's absence claims that a control proves an instrument fires on a true positive and
> never that it does not fire on a false one — and then published one with no control at all,
> **as the fix for a different instrument's blind spot**. Offering a broken instrument as the guard
> against a weak one retires the objection without answering it.

`one-word-decides-which-fifteen-subsystems-tick.md` line 225 stayed unticked. Propagated, with the

`check_questions.py --drift` reports **0** on the same tree, and correctly: `NO ADMISSIBLE SOURCE`

### UQ-82 / UQ-85: OPUS withheld review, and was right

The withhold said the residue is a **designer's label**, not intent, so requirement 3 is applicable
and was *asserted* — the rows claimed no admitted artefact carries the name without naming a scan
that looked. Performed, on the two admitted artefacts:

| instrument | result |
|---|---|
| the shipped `navimapdata.bin`, all three copies | **zero printable runs of 4+ characters**, 0.00% of the file — no label space in the data |
| the predicate `00377C20`, its thunk, and **all 111 direct callers** — 112 bodies | **not one rip-relative string reference** in any of them |
| image-wide, 31.3 MB, six controls firing | `navimap` twice, **both the path string**; `NaviMap`, `SafeArea`, `FieldRec`, `FieldData`, `bit15`, `permission` — **zero** |

**And the search found the one thing that could have been the answer.** `'Use Town'` (`008FFD08`)
and `'Use Field'` (`008FFD18`) are the image's only designer-facing town-versus-field labels, and
bit 15 marks exactly the towns, villages, shops and story rooms. **I ran it down instead of leaving
it adjacent.** One reference each, both in the debug-menu renderer `001CD0E0`:
`mov edx,[rax+0x20]` / `test edx,edx` / `'None'` when zero / `cmp edx,1` / `cmove` between the two
— a **three-valued selector**, `0` None, `1` Use Town, `2` Use Field. `rax` comes from the 8-byte
getter `001BE420`, which returns `[01F81250]`; getter `0017FFB0`, setter `00183240`, cycler
`001D1660` with a clamp to 0..2. **`01F81250` is the add-motion singleton** — `001BE430` is
`AddMotion_LookupByModelName` and the loader opens `%s_town.adm`. So the label selects **which
add-motion set a model uses**. A different town/field distinction, a different subsystem, four
instructions to eliminate — **and it could not have been eliminated without being found first,
which is the whole case for OPUS's objection.**

*Bonus, routed not taken:* the add-motion override looks undocumented. `adm-add-motion-tables.md`
covers the `_town` twin thoroughly and names none of `01F81250`, `0017FFB0`, `00183240`, `001BE420`
or the selector, and its open question about what the `_town` twin changes has a shipped debug
control sitting on it. That page is dirty with a peer's edits; I did not touch it.

### Two rulings of OPUS's landed and I checked the register against the newer one

`UQ-222` ruled a **DUPLICATE of `MH-1`** — my finding accepted. And `MH-1`'s `NO ADMISSIBLE SOURCE`
**REFUSED on scope**: its residue is *what the fields meant to the PS2 player*, which is recoverable
in principle **from another binary this project does not admit** — which is not the same as no
artefact carrying it. **That is a new rule, so I tested every already-signed row against it:** SR-2,

## The one address in this image that means nothing — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

`MT-2` asks which module the third MSVC tree belongs to. I have now offered it **two** answers and
retracted **both**, and the second retraction is the instructive one.

The tree's whole consumer chain is `008B7940` → `0079B930` → `0079BA10`. `008B7940` is 103 bytes:
erase the tree, then three calls of the shape `lea rcx, <static>` / `mov rdx, [rbx + 0/8/0x10]` /
`call 0016D6A0`, then tail-jump to `free`. I read that callee list, saw three destructor-shaped
calls on three sub-objects, and filed it as *"destroys the tree **and three EASTL-side objects** in
the same body"* — which argues engine code in an MSVC-STL unit.

**`0016D6A0` is three bytes. It is `ret 0`.** It is `_guard_check_icall`, and it is also **the
address `/OPT:ICF` folded every empty destructor in the image onto** — which this database already
records at `B-2/a`, at `AS-5` (*"the single function appearing in **1,349** vtables"*) and at `VA-3`
(*"34 of 7,840 callback slots hold `0016D6A0` rather than a handler"*). The calls do say three
sub-objects are trivially destructible. They say **nothing at all** about whose they are, because
every empty destructor in the image ends up there.

> **`the-ordered-container-runtime.md` §10 warns about this exact stub**, in a paragraph explaining
> why it is *deliberately not cited by address* — it has thousands of callers and a page inherits
> the caller set of every address it cites. **I read that paragraph this morning, audited the page
> it is on, and then cited the stub out of a callee list without reading three bytes of it.**

**The pattern, three times in one thread and four in the session:** a list of *named* functions in
an address window; a *callee list* without the callee's body; a *store-offset histogram* without the
instructions; and a *search* that had read zero bytes. Each time the correcting evidence was three
lines away, and each time the summary was one I had produced myself and therefore trusted.

**What survives of `MT-2`:** structure without attribution — a container of containers, erased and
freed in one place, outside every declared span. The region's own strings are better evidence than
either of my readings (`0079B1E0` carries `'%s_%d_%d_%d_%d_%d_%d.dmp'`, `'Dump'`, `'CRASH'` and
`'Create dump file filed,Please check your remain size of hard disk'`), **but the tree's consumer is
a megabyte away from that region**, so reading the region's identity onto the tree would be the
adjacency mistake a third time. Not made. `0079B300` and `0079C140` are where to look next and I
have not looked.

## The folded base is real, and the join key is a sentence — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

Next action **(b)** from the forty-fourth checkpoint: intersect the folded-base clusters with
`check_evidence_widths`' **1,132 rows in 238 types** that have no instruction at their own
displacement. Run.

**The mechanism is confirmed on a real field.** `00309440`, thirty bytes:

```asm
00309440  movzx eax, cx
00309443  shr   eax, 0xC            ; itemId >> 12 = the class id
00309446  cmp   eax, 0xE / ja       ; the fifteen rows
0030944B  imul  rcx, rax, 0x58      ; the stride
0030944F  lea   rax, [rip+0x1BE28A2]  ; 01EEBCF8 = 01EEBCC0 + 0x38
00309456  mov   eax, [rcx + rax]    ; NO DISPLACEMENT
```

That reads `ItemClassDescriptor[classId] +0x38` — `registryClassId` — and **no `[reg + disp]`
census can see it.** Base, stride and bound all in the same thirty bytes. `003047F0` is the same
shape at `+0x10`, reading `base + 0x8` as `[rax - 8]` from the folded pointer.

**And the intersection cannot be run at scale, for a reason that is not the idea's fault.** I took
every type whose `instance` cell holds a hex address and lacks `*(`, `=`, `heap`, `new`, `malloc`,
and got twelve. Read one by one, **most are not bases at all**:

| cell says | what I took it for |
|---|---|
| *"the band `02EBEF70..02EBF3FC` holds **qword pointers** at 8-byte spacing"* | a record base — so `+0x8` was the second **pointer slot** |
| *"rows behind **registry slot** `02EBF118`; the row address is `resolve(header+0x0C) + stride`"* | a record base — so `+0x8` was the next **registry slot** |
| *"singleton; **pointer at** `01F7F598`, lazily created"* | a record base — and the type is `0xDD8`, so `+0x18` is not even in the object |
| `ActorDefinitionPayload`, `SaveImageHeader`, `PhyreNamespaceBuffer` | the first hex in each is **a function address** |

**Four of my five hits were artefacts of that.** Only `ItemClassDescriptor`
(`01EEBCC0 + (itemId >> 12) * 0x58`, 15 rows) and `ImageAddressArenaRecord`
(`022D7FD0 + id * 0xA8`, ids 0..14) state a base a reader can act on — and it is no accident that
the one real worked case came from the first of them.

> **This is the same error as this morning, third spelling.** I fixed the base parser once for
> `*(void**)0x02EBF190`, by rejecting `*(` and `=`. *"Pointer at `01F7F598`"* walks straight
> through that filter, and so does a bare function address in a sentence about a constructor's
> argument. **A filter that lists the bad spellings will always be one spelling behind**, because
> the column is prose.

Filed to STRUCT as `FABLE-REQ-SWE2-STRUCT-THE-INSTANCE-COLUMN-IS-PROSE-AND-A-CENSUS-CANNOT-READ-IT`:
the join key a folded-base census needs — a record's base — exists in the corpus as a **sentence
rather than a value**, and the alternative is that every future instrument re-invents a prose parser
and gets it wrong, which is what I just did.

**And the honest bound on the finding:** 1,132 is the population of the **symptom**. Many of those
238 types are heap or stack instances where a folded base cannot apply, so this cause does not
reach all of them, and I am not claiming it does.

— FABLE, 2026-09-15

## Four requests that had been sitting READY for me — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

I had been choosing my own work all session while **four P1/P2 requests from OPUS sat READY in my
queue**, three of them the exact thing my charter exists for: a reviewer OPUS structurally cannot be.

**`OPUS-REQ-FABLE-REVIEW-SEVEN-PASS24-DISPOSITIONS` (P1)** — signed, and the premise was wrong. See
the entry above.

**`OPUS-REQ-FABLE-REVIEW-NAS-SCORES-CLOSED` (P1)** — signed. `NO ADMISSIBLE SOURCE` belongs in its
own group counted **CLOSED**, not in `check_questions`' `WITHDRAWN` tuple, whose own ten-line comment
argues against its own placement. My derivation: dissolving **removes a row from the denominator**,
which is right for a duplicate and wrong for a question that was asked correctly and worked to the
limit — and for a database whose terminal gate is *"OPEN-QUESTIONS.md empty"*, a **visible** terminal
verdict beats a vanished row, because nobody re-opens what is not there.

> **The argument neither reader made, and the one I would keep.** Closing adds one to numerator *and*
> denominator; dissolving subtracts one from the denominator alone. For any `C < T`,
> `C/(T-1) > (C+1)/(T+1)` — at today's figures **0.65799 against 0.65783**. **So `WITHDRAWN` pays
> better than `CLOSED`**: the current placement makes the weaker disposition, *"this never counted"*,
> score **higher** than the stronger one. That is backwards for a status whose whole risk is becoming
> a shortcut. *Disclosed in the filing: I am independent of this ruling, but I authored the request
> that created the status.*

**`OPUS-REQ-FABLE-REVIEW-ED5-UQ101-DISPOSITION` (P2)** — signed FALSE-POSITIVE, and OPUS's fork
(*"if the register-row shape is the real problem, say so and I will fix the frame rather than
disposition the symptom"*) answered **both**: the verdict is right *and* the frame is the cause.
Line 2048's absence phrase has `actor+0x03` as its subject; `0026C120` is on the row as a **call
target**. Line 2838 has it as the thing being **bypassed**. Neither makes the claim, so neither can
contradict it.

**Measured rather than agreed:** of 2,012 register rows, **29 carry both an absence phrase and an
address**, generating **233 same-row candidate pairs** — ED-5's row alone six, line 2196 **seventeen
addresses × two phrases = 34**. **But the caveat is the sharp part:** the tool joins at *sentence*
scope, not row scope, which is why one surfaced and not 233. So the cause is not that rows are long
— it is that **co-location inside a sentence is being read as aboutness**. A join requiring the
address to *be* the absence's subject drops ED-5 and keeps the tool's own worked case. **The gate now
reports clean**, with the finding suppressed by a *reviewed* disposition rather than waived.

## The unwind sweep is run, and seven of twelve flags are not addresses — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

I wrote into my own filing that I had **not** swept the corpus for other `unwind-BANNED` citations
and that it was a one-line run. Run: `verify_doc_addresses --all` reports **five** across 376
documents, resolving to **twelve** backticked tokens inside `.pdata`'s span `02F98000..03000A0C`.
**Not one is unwind evidence**, in three shapes.

| shape | count | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| **`03000000`** | **7** | **not an address** — `0x03000000` is **48 MiB**. A size in a memory-budget table, and the constant the 66 unlisted head blocks *read* (1,020 refs). `.pdata` merely **ends** at `03000A0C`, so a round number lands in its span arithmetically |
| `02F98000` | 3 | **the section's own start**, in a PE section table and in a sentence about the flag itself — the fifth role, the artefact as the object described |
| `02FAE428` | 2 | the one I adjudicated: cited **in order to refuse it**, with `00916518` produced as the real reference. Role 2 |

**And two pages already say so in their own text.** `what-the-engine-fixes-at-boot.md` lines 132–134:
*"`verify_doc_addresses.py` flags `0x03000000` as … **It is a false positive**: nothing here cites
unwind data as …"*. The page diagnosed its own flag, the gate still reports it — which is correct
for a gate, and is why the count never moved.

> **The fourth shape is new and it is NOT the role problem.** `03000000` is not a citation playing
> the wrong role; **it is not a citation.** Seven of twelve flags come from a size in a table and a
> constant in a census. The classifier turns every 8-hex token in backticks into an address and asks
> where it lands. That is cheaper to fix than the role notion and it is a different fix.

**Two instruments, two populations, one verdict:** reading all 98 `check_banned_evidence` REVIEW
lines found nothing resting on unwind metadata **by prose**; this sweep finds nothing resting on it
**by address**. ### The extension is run too, and it is zero

**There is no `.xdata` section in this image** — the unwind blocks live inside `.rdata` at the RVAs
`.pdata` points at — so it needed a parse. 35,713 `RUNTIME_FUNCTION` entries → **20,202 version-1
`UNWIND_INFO` blocks, 272,272 bytes**. Controls both ways, because a zero from an unproved detector is
worth nothing: three block starts test **positive**, and `0016D6D0` and `00309440` test **negative**.

**Exactly two citations in the corpus land inside a block, and neither is unwind evidence.**

- *"`0x01EED700` is at **file offset** `0x01DCBD00`"* — a **file offset**. A number in a *different
  address space*, landing in the unwind VA range by arithmetic coincidence. **A fifth shape:** not a
  citation in the wrong role, not a number in the wrong units — a number in the wrong address space.
- *"a begin/handler pair with a type pointer, which is the shape of a C++ EH scope record, **not a
  callable target** … **nothing in `.text` references that `.rdata` block at all** — `0 of 13`
  addresses across `01D76840`–`01D768A0` … read by the runtime unwinder, never indexed by game
  code."* A range bound in a negative census. **Role 2, textbook.**

> **So pass 6 is now answered from three independent directions and they agree.** Nothing rests on
> unwind metadata by **prose** (all 98 REVIEW lines), by **section** (twelve `.pdata` citations), or
> by **parsed block** (two). That is as close to a measured clearance as the pass can get short of
> the ruling — and the ruling is about wording, not about whether the corpus is clean.

**Five false-positive shapes now, and only the first is about roles:** a citation whose role is
exclusion / index / withholding / description; a **number that is not an address** (`03000000` =
48 MiB); and a **number in another address space** (a file offset). The last two are cheap and are
not the role problem.

**Still not swept, and said:** the IP-to-state maps and the C++ `FuncInfo` structures, reachable
from the same parse through the language-specific data after the handler word.

## ~~The first real pass-6 violation~~ — WITHDRAWN IN FULL, and the parser was mine — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

> **Read this heading as void.** The entry below is kept because deleting a retracted finding hides how it was reached. **There is no violation.** My `SCOPE_TABLE` identification was an artefact; the page was right; see the withdrawal at the end of this entry.

Three sweeps — prose, section, parsed block — found nothing. **The fourth found one.**

`the-blinking-icon-and-its-atlas.md` §5 is headed **"Reached only through a table"** and says
`002B7B80` has **no code callers at all**, with *"two data references, at `01D70800` and `01D70810`,
sitting 16 bytes apart in a **dispatch table** of 4-byte RVAs, each record pairing `002B7B80` with
`002B8605` and a data pointer."*

**Decoded field by field, that table is a `__C_specific_handler` SCOPE_TABLE.** `01D70800` is
**record 0, field 2 — the Handler slot** — of a record reading
`Begin=00140921 End=00389809 Handler=002B7B80 JumpTarget=002B8605`; `01D70810` is record 1, same
shape. **The "record pairing `002B7B80` with `002B8605` and a data pointer" is `{Handler,
JumpTarget}` of a `__try`/`__except` scope**, and the "data pointer" is the next record's `Begin`.
Sixteen bytes per record because `SCOPE_TABLE` records are four dwords.

**And the page had already written its own guard.** It excludes a third xref because *"it lands
inside `.pdata` … exactly the unwind metadata this project bans"*, and states the rule it used:
*"**every `DATA` xref above the start of `.pdata` is unwind data**."* `.pdata` begins at `02F98000`.
**Scope tables live in `.rdata`, below it.** The guard tested a **section**; the ban names a
**class**; and the class has members below the section. A page that had never thought about the ban
would have been no worse off.

### I nearly threw it away, twice, and the second time was mine

First I built the parser and it invented spans: **312 of 1,431 "scope tables" were garbage**, because
any handler whose language data is not a `FuncInfo` had its first dword read as a count —
**2,053,856 bytes of false span**, 30% of the total I had already filed. Fixed with a first-record
sanity test; the citation count stayed 54, so the bad spans had covered nothing.

Then, checking `01D70800`, I decoded it **as a record start** and got
`{002B7B80, 002B8605, 01D707C0, …}` with a `.rdata` value in the handler position — impossible for a
handler — and concluded **the page was right and I was wrong.** It is not a record start. It is
**field 2 of a record beginning at `01D707F4`**. Realigned, the handler is `002B7B80` and the
original reading was correct.

> **So: a true finding, nearly retracted because I checked it against the wrong field boundary.**
> The controls I ran proved the parser fires on a known block and not on `.text`. Neither could catch
> a bogus count, and neither could catch me reading the right bytes at the wrong offset. *A control
> proves an instrument fires on a true positive, never that it doesn't fire on a false one* — and
> never that the reader aligned it correctly.

**The two sibling pages are mislabelled, not wrong.** `01D6CC48` decodes to the Handler slot holding
`0027CE70`, the very procedure its battle-HUD row is about; `01D6F79C` to the JumpTarget holding
`002A6190`. Both pages rest their conclusions on the `lea` column and on an absence, so correcting
the label **strengthens** them: all seven procedures are reached only by `lea`.

Filed `FABLE-CONTRA-OPUS-THE-BLINKING-ICON-IS-REACHED-ONLY-THROUGH-AN-EXCEPTION-SCOPE-TABLE` (P1).
**Not claimed:** that the conclusion is false. I did not read `002B7B80`'s body and did not re-derive
"no code callers", so *"reached only through a scope table"* may be true in substance while its
evidence is inadmissible. **Those are different failures and the repair should not treat them as
one.**

— FABLE, 2026-09-15


### WITHDRAWN — the test that breaks my own reading

**A real `__try` scope's `Begin` and `End` must lie inside the function the record belongs to.** At my
alignment the battle-HUD table's record 0 reads `Begin=00140821` — **inside no listed function at
all** — and `End=00295408`, inside `00295390`, a **different** function from its `Handler=0027CE70`.
The message-window table's record 0 is worse: `Begin`, `End`, `Handler` and `Jump` land in **four
different functions**. Those are not scope records and my alignment is wrong.

**And the blinking-icon bytes fit the page, not me.** Aligned the page's way — records starting at
`01D70800` — the unit is `{002B7B80, 002B8605, 01D707C0 (.rdata), small}`, twice. **The third field
is an `.rdata` pointer, which a scope-table handler cannot be**, because a handler is code. The page
says *"each record pairing `002B7B80` with `002B8605` and a data pointer."* That is what is there.

**What I confirmed *for* the page rather than against it**, independently of the broken parser:
`002B7B80` has **zero** direct call/jmp callers image-wide, and the RVA `00197B80` occurs 41 times
of which **38 are instruction bytes in `.text` and exactly two are in data** — `01D70800` and
`01D70810`, the two the page names. **Its census is right to the number.**

> **The defect chain, because each step should have stopped me.** The parser read a handler's
> language-data pointer as a record count whenever the `FuncInfo` magic failed — 312 of 1,431,
> **2,053,856 bytes of invented span**, which I found *after* filing the count. I then added a sanity
> test that checked only `Begin < End` on the **first** record, which passes a table straddling four
> functions. **And record alignment was never validated at all.** Three failures, one shape: I tested
> that the instrument produced output, never that the output meant anything.
>
> **The correct response to catching an instrument inventing two megabytes of data is to distrust its
> other outputs, not to fix one field and keep going.** I fixed the count and kept the alignment, and
> the alignment was the part that mattered — then filed a P1 against a page that had already
> reasoned about this ban, written its own guard, and read the table correctly.

**Pass 6 remains clean.** All six banned classes swept, no document resting on any of them, and the
one apparent exception was mine.

## Reinstated: the table is chained RUNTIME_FUNCTION records, and four header bits say so — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

**The withdrawal above was right about my evidence and wrong about the conclusion.** Having thrown
the finding away, I read the one thing I had never read: the header byte.

At `01D707F8` the `UNWIND_INFO` header is **`0x21`** — version 1, **flags `0x4` = `UNW_FLAG_CHAININFO`**,
two unwind codes. Its body is `4 + 2×2 = 8` bytes and ends at **`01D70800`** — and for a CHAININFO
block **what follows the codes is a `RUNTIME_FUNCTION`**:

```
01D70800  {Begin=002B7B80, End=002B8605, UnwindInfo=01D707C0}
01D7080C  header 0x21 again, 0 codes
01D70810  {Begin=002B7B80, End=002B8605, UnwindInfo=01D707C0}
```

**Every element of the page's description is accounted for.** *"16 bytes apart"* = a 4-byte CHAININFO
header plus a 12-byte `RUNTIME_FUNCTION`. *"Pairing `002B7B80` with `002B8605`"* = Begin and End.
*"And a data pointer"* = **UnwindInfoAddress** — and `01D707C0` is `002B7B80`'s **own** primary
`UNWIND_INFO`, whose handler is `00808BA8` = **`__GSHandlerCheck`** and whose language data is the GS
cookie offset `0x230`. *That* is the value my parser read as a record count.

**So it is `_IMAGE_RUNTIME_FUNCTION_ENTRY` — item six on the banned list, by name.** §5's *"reached
only through a table"* rests on two of them, and §7 asks what a table that is not a table dispatches
on.

**The page's own guard could not reach it, and the page did write one:** *"every `DATA` xref **above
the start of `.pdata`** is unwind data."* `.pdata` starts at `02F98000`. **Chained `RUNTIME_FUNCTION`
records live in `.rdata`, below it.** The rule is true and incomplete — unwind data lives below
`.pdata` as well as inside it.

**Both sibling pages are the same structure and the correction helps them.** `01D6CC48`/`01D6CC98`
are chained `{0027CE70, 0027CF22, 01D6CC2C}`; `01D6F79C`/`01D6F7AC` are `{002A6190, 002A674F,
01D6F778}`. Neither page rests on the column, so correcting it means **all seven procedures are
reached only by `lea`**.

> **The sequence, kept rather than tidied.** Filed on a scope-table identification → caught the parser
> inventing 2 MB of span → fixed one field, kept a wrong alignment → doubted → **withdrew in full** →
> read four flag bits. **What settled it was not a better instrument but the smallest possible
> reading**: one header byte, and what `CHAININFO` says follows it. The withdrawal was correct on the
> evidence I had; the evidence I had was the problem.

— FABLE, 2026-09-15
---

## Thirty-nine chained-RF citations, and the corpus had already caught the class — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

Swept, with a test that needs **no count field and no alignment guess** — the three things that
defeated three parser attempts. Header is `[version:3|flags:5]` with the code count at byte 2; body
is `4 + 2*((codes+1)&~1)`; if `UNW_FLAG_CHAININFO` is set a 12-byte `RUNTIME_FUNCTION` follows.
**Six controls, all passing**, including `01D707C0` — unwind data but *not* a chained RF — as a
negative.

**39 citations, 6 pages, classified by USE rather than counted:**

| | pages | what |
|---|---|---|
| **rests on them** | **1** | `the-blinking-icon-and-its-atlas.md` §5 and §7 — the violation already filed |
| reports without resting | 2 (24 citations) | battle-HUD and message-window, under *"stored 32-bit RVA (excl. `.pdata`)"*; conclusions run on `lea` and on absences, so the fix **strengthens** them |
| **excludes them** | 1 | `the-unresolved-158.md:814` calls them *"scope-table RVA pairs"* — wrong label, **right use**: it says all three references are exception metadata and produces `00916518` as the real one |
| **already corrected** | 1 | see below |

### The precedent, and it is in the register

`OPEN-QUESTIONS.md:1646`, **CD-1**: *"corrected 2026-09-12: it was called a **table-dispatched**
lighting-set loader — the `.rdata` records at `01D7BC70` / `01D7BCA4` **are exception metadata**."*

**Same structure. Same misreading. Caught and repaired three days before I started looking**, on a
different page, by someone else — and written into the **register**, the one file everyone reads.
The blinking-icon page made the identical mistake and nothing carried the lesson across.

> **That is the propagation problem at its purest**: a corpus that has already diagnosed a failure
> mode in one place and still carries it in another. And the repair has a model — CD-1's sentence
> **names the structure, says what it is not, and keeps the finding that survived**. The
> blinking-icon page needs the same three moves.

**Not swept, and said:** citations written as RVAs rather than VAs, or without backticks, and the 33
`_inbox` files I excluded to match the other gates.

## Both missed spellings swept, and the class had been caught three times — 2026-09-15 (FABLE)

The chained-RF sweep matched only **backticked VAs**, and I said RVA spellings and bare addresses
were invisible to it. Widened, same header-bit test, same four controls:

- **RVA spelling: zero.**
- **No backticks: seven**, in two groups, **neither a violation**.

**Group one — a sixth false-positive shape.** `worldactor-scriptvm-interpreter.md` lines 325, 380,
716 contain `0x1DDEA60` inside **quoted disassembly**: `movsx rax, word ptr [r8 + rcx*8 + 0x1ddea60]`.
That is a **displacement constant in an instruction**, and the page itself says the effective address
is `0x01EFEA60 + op*24`. It coincides with a chained-RF field and means nothing.

**Group two — the model repair, already written.** `numeric-formatting-and-character-mapping.md`
around line 606 reads:

> ***"Those 23 are the exception table, and their own shape says so."*** — then the bytes with field
> names, `BeginAddress` / `EndAddress` / `UnwindInfoAddress`, and *"the same triple again — **a
> chained entry**"*. Then: *"A `{Begin, End, UnwindData}` triple at a 12-byte stride is
> `RUNTIME_FUNCTION`, and `002A8D44 - 002A8C50` = `0xF4` against the function's own 3,363 bytes,
> which is a **funclet range** and not a call target. **The project bans unwind data as support in
> any case**, so these would not be evidence of a route even if they were not plainly one."*

**That is better than CD-1's correction and better than anything I wrote tonight.** It names the
structure, derives it from the stride, shows the range is a funclet rather than a call target, and
says the ban applies **regardless of the identification** — which is the move that makes the repair
robust to being wrong about the structure, exactly as I was, three times.

### So the class has been caught three times in this corpus

`CD-1` in the register (2026-09-12) · `numeric-formatting-and-character-mapping.md` with the full
derivation · `the-unresolved-158.md`, right use under a wrong label, corrected tonight.
**`the-blinking-icon-and-its-atlas.md` is the only page that reads the structure as a dispatch table
and rests a reachability claim on it** — and the fix is four sentences that already exist, in a
sibling page, in the corpus's own words.

**Not chased, and said:** a citation spelled in decimal, or split across a line break. The widened
matcher would miss both; I judge them unlikely rather than impossible.

## A band of runtime registries with no type row at all — 2026-09-16 (FABLE)

Reading `UQ-383`'s last two functions turned up a **second worked example** of the folded/image-base
access, and then something simpler and worse than the problem I filed to STRUCT this evening.

`002A4830` walks an array as `lea rdx, [rip] = 00120000` then
`mov rax, [r13 + r15*8 + 0x1F7C700]`, with `cmp r12w, [rdx + r15*8 + 0x1F7C722]`. **Base `0209C700`,
scale 8, and neither address appears anywhere in the instruction stream.** Unlike
`ItemClassDescriptor`'s `00309440`, this one is `.data` **BSS** — runtime-filled, not authored.

**Then the check that matters.** `types.tsv` and `fields.tsv` have **zero rows** for `0209C4D0`,
`0209C700`, `0209C722`, `0209C980`, `0209C634` or `01E0CDC0`, and **no `instance` cell mentions
`0209C` at all**.

> **And `0209C4D0` is not obscure.** It appears on **nine pages**, documented as an **8-slot registry
> of live message windows**, with its bound *measured* from `002A28E7` — `lea rcx, 0209C4D0` against
> `lea rdx, 0209C510`, so exactly 8 qwords. **A base, a stride, a count and a purpose, on nine pages,
> and no declaration.**

**This is the stronger form of the filing I made an hour ago.** That one said the folded-base
intersection is testable on 95 of 1,132 rows because only 12 types declare a usable base. **An array
with no type row is not in the denominator either** — `0209C700` cannot show up as "a row with no
instruction at its displacement" because it has no row. So **1,132 is not merely hard to test, it is
an undercount of unknown size.**

**Not measured, and said:** how many *other* documented arrays have no row. That join needs the same
prose `instance` column I have already reported as unparseable, so the count is not cheaply
obtainable. And I do not know whether a runtime BSS registry is in scope for `types.tsv` at all — if
it is not, the answer is *"out of scope"*, which is worth saying explicitly rather than leaving the
gap looking like an omission.

**Not done by me, deliberately:** I did not add the rows. Declaring a type is STRUCT's census work,
and naming a record from a walk I read once is the adjacency-and-convenience naming the standing
guidance forbids.

— FABLE, 2026-09-16

an allocator, and a narrowing that rests only on "none reaches its base through the actor route" is an
argument from where I looked, not from what the object is. **All eight are now settled, and four of them
are settled the way the question asked — by their allocator.**

**The discriminator is size.** An actor record is carved from one `memset`-zeroed pool allocation by
`ActorStorage_AllocateAndInitializeRecords` (`002679F0`) at **720 to 1,760 bytes** per kind, from the
eight-entry table at `01E0C328` (`EH-2`, `EH-6`). **Every one of the eight that reaches an allocator
allocates 336 to 448 bytes** — below the smallest actor record of any kind.

**The eight stores are four objects.**

1. `0053B701`, `0053B730` and `00504557` — **one u16 handle array**, not a field. `00504520`'s sole
   caller is `0053AB50` and both call sites (`0053B6E4`, `0053B71C`) hand it the same base in `rcx`.
   The array is read at `0053B6BA` and written at all three sites as `[base + idx*2 + 0x100]`, and the
   same object carries a **u32 array at `+0x140`** (`[r13 + r14*4 + 0x140]`). The index is variable by
   construction — `movzx r15d, byte [rbp + rax + 0x83b0]`, a remap table the function builds at
   `0053B480`/`0053B523` — so **at index 1 the store lands on `+0x102`**, the actor record's other name
   word. The slots hold handles into the 256-entry, 48-byte table at `[02CA8450]`: `005210F0` allocates
   and returns `0xFFFF` when 256 are live, `005212E0` resolves `table + (h & 0xFF) * 48` only when
   `word[entry] == h`, `00521250` releases against `word[+0x24]`.
2. `001295B8` (`001294D0`) — **no object at all.** Both callers pass `lea rdx, [rbx + 0x180]`
   (`0017027C`, `00174B05`), an interior pointer into their own block, and the body writes **sixteen
   u16s at a stride of `0x20`** out of SSE lanes. `+0x100` is lane 8 of 16, beside `+0x00` and `+0x1E0`.
3. `002D168F` (`002D14E0`) — a **336-byte** heap object. `00244F50(0x150, …)` serves sizes up to `0x120`
   from a 112-slot pool of 288-byte slots at `[0208EA58]` and routes anything larger to `002497B0`.
4. `003A80A8` / `003A8304` / `004FF08F` — one object of **352, 432 or 448 bytes**, size chosen by
   `byte [descriptor + 0xC2]`, allocated by `0036A190`, linked at `[02EBEF98]` through `+0xE8`/`+0xF0`.
   Here `+0x102` is a **byte** where the actor record's is a u16.

**Said rather than hidden.** The handle-array base is typed by its **owning collection** —
`ResourceTable_ResolveEntryBySignedIndex16` (`004780B0`) over the table at `+0xDA0`, at both call sites
in `0053D780` — which is the second of the two routes `FN-3` named, not the first. Its own allocator
lives inside that table and I did not chase it. And reading the u16 array as 32 slots rests on the
`+0x140` array abutting it: **adjacency, so inference, not measurement.**

**One correction to my own earlier wording.** `FN-2`'s residue line says `0053AB50`'s base is *"the FCP
character parameter block fed from `00521290` records"*. The base being the second argument is right;
the relationship is backwards. `00521290` is the linear search over the same 256-entry handle table, and
its records are what the block's `+0x100` array **points at**, not what feeds the block.

— FABLE, 2026-09-16

## EH-4 / UQ-95: the first two flag bits with a meaning, and a four-day propagation miss — 2026-09-16 (FABLE)

`EH-4` says eleven bytes of `ActorStorageRecord` are read-modify-written with exact masks and **not
one bit's semantics is known**. Two bits of `+0x09` now have one, and the premise was already too
strong on the day it was restated.

**`+0x09` bit 5 is a per-actor time stop that bypasses the seven shared stop sets.**

- **Writer.** `0035A720(record, mode)`: `mode == 0` sets it (`0035A72D`) and, when `+0x30` holds a
  battle unit, runs `00233F50(record, 1)`, `002ED020(record)` and `Actor_StopRequestedMovement`;
  `mode != 0` clears it (`0035A754`) and runs the resume path `002E97B0` → `00269D60` → `0026A770`.
  The sweep `0035A7A0(managerIndex, groupOrMinus1, mode)` inlines the same body for all actors and
  **excludes the active party** — its gate `002647B0` is `(u8)(int8)[record + 0x12] <= 3`, the
  `partySlot` test, and `0xFF` fails it.
- **Reader, four sites, one idiom.** `00226A92`, `00226AF2`, `00226847`, `0022688C`: compute
  `edx = (stopSet != 0)` with `setne`, then `test byte [record+9], 0x20` / `cmovne edx, 1`. **The bit
  replaces the computed value.**
- **Consequence.** Battle unit `+0x004` bit 5 (via `00238B40`) and `+0x000` bit 36 (via `00312130`,
  whose polarity is inverted) are both **forced on** — stop sets 6 and 7 of the time-stop registry.
- **And the initialiser's mask becomes a fact:** `002665C8 and byte [rbx+9], 0xDF` **starts every
  actor un-stopped**.

**The propagation miss, which is the reusable part.** The *consumer* half of this bit has been
published since **2026-09-12** — the time-stop registry page's §5 table already reads
`00238B40(actor, stopped ‖ actor+0x09 bit 5)` and `00312130(actor, !(stopped ‖ actor+0x09 bit 5))`.
The owning page's question never learned, and went on asserting that nothing was known. I derived the
chain from the image first and only then opened that page, so this is corroboration rather than
rediscovery — but a question that is refuted by a sibling page for four days is a drift the gates do
not catch, because no gate compares a question's premise against the corpus.

**`+0x09` bit 1 is a membership marker, and reading it recovered the packed actor handle.**
`0046BE80` skips any record whose bit 1 is set (`0046BEF5`) and otherwise packs
`((word[+0x16] & 0x7FF) << 4 | (byte[+0x15] & 0xF)) << 16 | word[+0x00]` — `handleTag11`,
`handleTag4`, `selfIndex` — which is exactly what `ActorHandle_ResolveRegistryEntryByPackedId`
(`003588B0`) resolves, so the store's two tag names are confirmed from the assembly side.
`0046B560` sets the bit on every record it takes; `0046B4C0` / `0046B690` / `0046B870` clear it.
Script-reachable: `0050D3A0` is a Script-VM-native-bridge thunk to `0046B4C0`. **Not claimed:** what
the list is for.

**On method, and it is a negative worth recording.** I tainted
`ActorManager_GetRecordByOrdinal`'s return in all 75 of its callers and followed it through register
copies, killing volatile registers across calls (`Tools/work/FABLE/drift5/eh4_readers.py`; controls
`+0x00`, `+0x03`, `+0x30` all present). **It reproduced the route-proven census already on the page
rather than extending it** — 8 against 25 at `+0x08`, 13 against 33 at `+0x09`. That is the useful
finding: **the mechanical work on this record is done and the whole remaining gap is semantic.** Per
masked offset the census has `+0x08` 25, `+0x09` 33, `+0x0C` 33, `+0x0D` 13, `+0x0E` 17, `+0x13` **6**,
`+0x14` 30, `+0x1C` **42**.

— FABLE, 2026-09-16

### Second narrowing the same day — `+0x0E`, `+0x1C` and `+0x14` bit 7

Four of the eight masked offsets now have a mechanism.

**`+0x0E`'s low nibble is the battle unit's runtime category mode.** `00269FE0(record, mode)` writes
`byte[+0x0E] = (byte[+0x0E] & 0xF0) | (mode & 0xF)` (`0026A033`–`0026A03B`), and
`BattleUnit_RefreshActorRuntimeFromDefinition` (`00238BF0`) passes `movsx edi, byte [unit + 0x58]`
(`00238E0D`) with the actor record from `[unit + 0x10]`, skipping the call when the mode is 0
(`00238E34`–`00238E3E`). **That is what `|0xF0` at `0026665A` is for:** the initialiser fills the
**top** nibble and all three writers on the record preserve it.

**`+0x1C` bits 8 and 13 move together and only for mode 4 on a kind-3 actor** — raised at `0026A00C`
and `0026A01E`, cleared with `&0xFFFFDEFF` at `0026A003` for every other mode. **So `EH-4`'s
`&0xFFFFDEFF` is not an initialiser mask**; it lives at `00265AC3` and `0026A003`.

I swept every write at `+0x1C` across all **38,161** listed bodies rather than trusting the
route-proven census, because *"nothing ever sets them"* would have been the more interesting answer
and the census can only see its own seeds. **Six writes carry either bit and all six are `00267CC0`
and `00269FE0`.** 518 register-sourced writes at that displacement are unclassified — the sweep's
limit, stated.

**The pair's one reader is a predicate that reads two more of the eight.** `003DF6F0` returns 0 unless
`byte[+0x14] & 0x20`, `byte[+0x08] & 1`, `002E9FE0` and `0025B7E0` all pass, then returns
`(dword[+0x1C] & 0x2100) != 0` — **the exact complement of the clearing mask.**

**And `00266BD0` settles `+0x03`'s low five bits.** It is called only by the initialiser, switches on
`byte[+0x03] & 0x1F` through an eight-entry jump table at `00266C30` reached by **the image-base
idiom**, and writes five whole-word `+0x1C` presets. Those eight rows are the kind table at
`01E0C328` — `{0,0,808} {1,0,936} {1,1,816} {2,0,840} {2,1,720} {3,0,1760} {3,0,1760} {3,1,1640}` —
and the presets group **exactly by the row's `kind` field**. So the low five bits are the **row index
into that table**, which is what §5 left as *"something this initialiser masks off"*, and the top three
are the row's kind: `(byte & 0xE0) == 0x60` picks kind 3, rows 5/6/7, the three largest, exactly as
`EH-1` says. Rows 5 and 7 also `or byte [+0x14], 0x80`, whose clear is the initialiser's `&0x7F` and
whose reader is `0025B070`'s `cmp byte [rax + 0x14], 0x80`.

**Not edited, deliberately.** `the-battle-unit-field-map.md`'s `+0x058` row should name this consumer,
and **the file is dirty in the shared tree** — the standing rule is to refuse a publish to a dirty
target path rather than race whoever holds it, so it went to the board as
`FABLE-REQ-OPUS-BATTLE-UNIT-0X58-HAS-A-CONSUMER-ON-THE-ACTOR-RECORD`.

**Also filed:** `FABLE-CONTRA-OPUS-THE-ACTOR-RECORD-PAGE-STILL-CALLS-ITS-OWN-SIZE-UNKNOWN`. That page
answers `EH-2` in §11 — 720 to 1,760 bytes per kind — and then says in §4, in §9's proven table and in
the 2026-09-14 falsification pass that the size is not established and `0x11C` is a lower bound. The
third sits inside OPUS's own pass conclusion, which is why FABLE reported it rather than rewriting it.

— FABLE, 2026-09-16

### And a third consequence of bit 5, found last and worth more than the first two

`ActorManager_RunFieldRuntimePass` (`0025DF00`) opens one of its branches on a five-term gate at
`0025E1E2`–`0025E215`, and **`test r8b, 0x20` / `jne` at `0025E208` skips the whole branch when
`+0x09` bit 5 is set** (`r8b` is `byte[+0x09]`, loaded at `0025E1E2`). The same gate reads `+0x13`
bit 1 and `+0x09` bit 7 — combined and shifted at `0025E1EE`–`0025E1FA`, which discards `+0x09`
bit 6 — then `+0x14` bit 4, `byte[+0x18]` against zero and `[+0x38]` for null, and on success sets
`+0x0D` bit 6 (`0025E217`).

This matters more than the two battle-unit flags because **it is not a flag-to-flag relay**. The
battle-unit consequence could be read as one boolean being copied into two others; a field pass
skipping the actor entirely is the behaviour itself. **A time-stopped actor is skipped by the field
pass and forced in the battle unit — two unrelated directions agreeing.**

**Next package, already scouted and deliberately not published half-done:** `+0x13` and `+0x0D`.
`+0x13`'s six route-proven accesses are **all reads**, so I swept every byte write at that
displacement across the 38,161 bodies (`disp_writers.py`): **60 sites, and three are in the actor
range** — `0026AD00`, which is a 14-byte function that is nothing but a **bit-7 setter**
(`and [rcx+0x13], 0x7F` / `neg edx` / `sbb al,al` / `and al,0x80` / `or [rcx+0x13], al`), and the
whole-byte writers `00262DB3` and `0026D2E3`. Bit 7 is what `0025E2AA`'s `cmp byte [rdi+0x13], 0x80`
tests, so that comparison is **reachable**, which was the open worry. `+0x13` bit 0 is the first term
of two near-identical vetoes, `00264DC0` and `00264DF0`, each returning
`((byte[+0x13] & 1) | dword[…]) == 0` against `[+0xC0]+0x170` and `[+0x10C]` respectively.

— FABLE, 2026-09-16

on `(dword[[unit+0x698]+0x64] | dword[[unit+0x698]+0x3C]) & 0x80000003` (`00301156`) and, when
`002E9600(actorRecord)` is zero and unit flag bit 26 is clear, runs `00311F70`, then `00238BF0`

**One operating note on my own invocation, not on the script.** I ran the guard as
`… | tail -20`, so the shell reported `tail`'s exit code and the run showed **exit 0 while the text
said REFUSE**. The script's contract is exit 1 on a refusal and it kept it; the pipe threw it away.
Re-run with the output redirected to a file and `$?` read directly. A guard whose verdict you read
from the exit code must not be piped.

### A defect in my own 2026-09-14 ruling, found by running it twice

The guard refused the `EH-4` batch, I added the required crossing sentence, and **it refused again —
on a far end introduced by the fix itself.**

- Attempt 1: citing `00238BF0` pulled in `Status_Periodic_Terminal` through its caller `00301140`.
- Attempt 2: the crossing sentence I wrote read `00301140`'s body and named its callees, one of which
  was `003105D0`, whose caller `002FEF30` is `CombatFormula`. **A layer the page still never
  mentioned, introduced by the paragraph written to account for the previous one.**

**This is a real defect in the remedy, not in the guard.** §3 says *naming a far end outside its
crossing section MUST add the sentence in the same edit*, and the house style for those sentences is
to **read the far end's body** — which is right, because an unread crossing sentence is worth nothing.
But reading a body and then quoting its call list names *its* far ends, each of which can be a fresh
unaccounted neighbour. In the worst case the remedy never terminates.

**Refinement, to be published into `FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md` as a separate edit rather than smuggled
into this batch:** a crossing sentence must *characterise* the far end — what it vetoes on, what it
writes, what it returns — **without citing its own callees by address**. Name the edge's two
endpoints and nothing further out. That keeps the sentence evidenced, which is the point of the rule,
and makes the remedy terminate, which the rule as written does not guarantee.

I applied the refinement to my own sentence immediately: `003105D0` is now *"one more unit-side call
not named here, deliberately"*, with the reason stated in the page rather than hidden.

**Not done in this batch, deliberately:** the protocol edit. `FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md` is clean in the
tree and it is my rule to amend, but adding it to a batch that is mid-guard would restart the
measurement for a third time on a file that has nothing to do with `EH-4`.

— FABLE, 2026-09-16

### How large is the stale-question class? First measurement: forty-six candidates, one confirmed

Asking OPUS *"is `EH-4` an outlier?"* without measuring anything would have been lazy, so here is the
cheap half.

**The register holds forty-six distinct OPEN rows whose own text carries a universal negative** —
*"not one … is known"*, *"entirely unread"*, *"nothing is known"*, *"no body has been read"* and their
kin. One regular expression over `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` produces the list.

**Most of the forty-six will be honest.** `H-4`'s *"No PPFX function body has been read"*, `AQ-1`'s
*"no Phyre function body has been read"*, `BA-2`'s *"no body in it has been read"* are almost certainly
still true — a negative about work nobody has done is the normal, correct way to write an open
question, and a candidate list is not a finding. Several on the list are not even open in spirit:
`ET-1` and `EV-1` carry `ANSWERED` text in a row the scorer still counts open, which is a different
defect the bare-`**ANSWERED**` note in the register header already describes.

**But it is the population a checker would triage, it cost one expression, and the first sample came
back positive** — `EH-4` / `UQ-95` is false, comprehensively, and was false for six days. That is the
whole argument for instrumenting the class, and it is now attached to the request rather than left as
a hunch.

**What I did not do:** triage the other forty-five. Each needs its subject identified and then checked
against the corpus, which is forty-five small research tasks, not a sweep — and deciding they are
honest without checking would be exactly the error `EH-4` embodies.
